To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) probability of recall of individual list items or idea units of texts can be predicted from the probability of recall of these items or units for young adults, with high reliability, and (b) for lists of words and of texts, the slopes of the functions relating item characteristics (e.g., frequency) to recall probability are reliably similar for the two age groups; for lists of paired associates the slopes of these functions are significantly larger for older adults as compared to the young adults

the probability of recall for individual items and idea units by older adults can be predicted by their probability of recall by young adults, and that the same item or idea unit characteristics predict recall probability in both age groups.
